chunks: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let false hope beguile them; so they will come to know.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about those distracted by worldly hope and pleasure?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological state of the disbelievers who are lulled into complacency by prolonged worldly enjoyment (tamattu') and the illusion of longevity (al-amal). It serves as a divine promise that their current delay in punishment is not an absence of justice, but a period of grace before the inevitable reckoning where they will finally 'know' the reality of their deeds.
